title: proxy-buffered-call-signal-loss-across-hosted-and-dedicated-paths
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Multiple customers reported that function/tool-call invocations return partial or missing structured outputs after passing through intermediate HTTP proxies or our dedicated edge. Failures are intermittent and correlate with proxy buffering + connection re-use, causing parser to miss the call-complete signal token that our structured output parser relies on.
environment: Observed on Hosted API (edge layer) and on Dedicated clusters behind customer proxies; appears in Private deployments when customer-side TLS-terminating proxies are present.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a function call that emits a final '\n__CALL_COMPLETE__\n' sentinel after JSON payload.
2) Send a streaming request through an HTTP/1.1 proxy with response buffering and connection reuse enabled.
3) Observe that in ~5-12% of requests the client-side parser never sees the sentinel and treats the response as truncated.
4) Reproduces more reliably under high concurrency and when proxy applies gzip or response chunk coalescing.
observed_behavior: Structured parser returns a parse error or returns only the partial JSON before the sentinel. Customers see missing function outputs, stale retry behavior, or duplicate fallbacks to simpler text completion. Errors spike on high-throughput routes and on tenants using customer-managed proxies.
expected_behavior: The streaming response should reliably deliver the sentinel/terminator indicating end-of-function output so the structured parser can validate and return a complete function result. No loss under normal proxy re-use or gzip coalescing.
customer_reports: Customer A (SaaS analytics): missing table schema from function call, production rollback initiated
Customer B (enterprise): duplicate retries and billing impact on Dedicated cluster
Customer C (regulated workload on Private): intermittent failure affecting nightly jobs
root_cause: Edge/proxy layers coalesce or buffer streaming chunks and, in some cases, strip or merge sentinel-aligned boundaries when response chunking + gzip compression + connection re-use occurs. Our parser assumes a strict sentinel-delimited boundary; when sentinel is merged into a larger buffered chunk and the chunk is truncated on retry, the sentinel can be missed. Additionally, an internal optimization in the streaming adapter dropped a trailing zero-length chunk in rare race conditions during proxy reconnect.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Recommend customers disable proxy response buffering or gzip on inference routes where feasible. 2) Deployed a backend server-side change to emit an idempotent JSON 'end' object as a fallback marker in addition to sentinel. 3) Rollout an emergency client-side parser patch that treats end-of-stream + partial JSON as retryable rather than returning a hard parse error.
permanent_fix_plan: 1) Harden streaming adapter: ensure stable framing by always flushing sentinel on its own chunk and enable chunk boundary protection in the runtime. 2) Update parser to tolerate merged/split sentinel markers and to reassemble across proxied chunk boundaries. 3) Add end-to-end tests emulating proxy buffering/gzip/connection-reuse to CI. 4) Ship runtime-1.29 with kernel fix and parser update.
rollout_plan: Canary parser update to 5% of Hosted routes for 48h, monitor sentinel-seen rate and customer errors; parallel rollout to Dedicated clusters with opt-in flag for early customers. Private customers provided patch bundle and migration guide.
notes: On 2026-03-11 we observed a 3x increase in parse-related incidents for routes using edge-nginx buffering.
Design discussed adding both sentinel and length-prefix framing; decided to implement tolerant parser + stronger runtime flush to minimize client changes.
Follow-up: add documented best-practices for customers running dedicated/private proxies (proxy tuning page).
